task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: role portability across team or context moves
methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units at useful power?
How should cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper roles be classified from play-by-play data?
How should portability be measured without deriving the label from the same outcome used to test it?
How should regression to the mean, landing-spot quality and small-sample instability be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Closest prior study. On 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether a connector's organizational function reproduced after a move (cut share rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653; cut-minus-drive rho=+0.314, p=0.002; drive rho=-0.278, p=0.007). Top cut tercile was 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) vs bottom 35% (median -0.039). LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005 from 5000 label shuffles. Record notes the drop-Gafford and top-3 checks and position splits. Its own limitation tags are [prior work] and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Connector diet x destination structural-gap match. Binary match rate 15.7%. Taxonomy connector subset n=19 gave delta match vs mismatch median +0.540 vs +0.069, p=0.156. Travel-check delta p=0.413. All-movers binary delta p=0.0283 (n=198) did not replicate as a continuous Spearman, which was -0.034 with p recorded as 0. Verdict null; failure type A_unanswerable; limited by [prior work].

DRIVE-as-BEST counter versus constrained mix, n=44. Observed gap -0.066 PPP (p=0.2175 vs B_fixed) with MDE 0.180 PPP at 80% power (SD about 0.34; 0.265 if SD about 0.5). Record states n=44 cannot distinguish a true null from an effect up to 0.18 PPP. Limited by [prior work] and [prior work].

Destination net-rating checks for movers (archive). Recorded result: 'underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality', with no numbers. Dropped from Paper 1. Failure type A_unanswerable; limited by [prior work] and [prior work]; related family [prior work][prior work].

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a diet-match or structural-gap-match binary against post-move delta in connector subsets and all movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with [prior work]. Connector subset was n=19; the all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman, which was reported with p=0, so the result is fragile and not the licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a DRIVE-based H2 PPP advantage over feasibility-constrained baselines
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with [prior work]. The observed gap was smaller than the MDE of 0.180 PPP at n=44, so the test could not distinguish a true null from a meaningful effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using destination on-court net-rating change to check whether portability relates to outcomes
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable and underpowered. The null result was reported only after correcting for landing-spot quality, and no sample or effect numbers were recorded. Dropped from Paper 1.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project ([prior work][prior work]) reported a positive cut-share association with post-move portability in a 92-mover sample, with a permutation-based p-value and a leave-one-out AUC of 0.622.

Three other attempts in the same area ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) were recorded as untestable because of small samples or large minimum detectable effects. Sample size and power were the dominant recorded failure mode in this area.
Destination-quality confounding was recorded as material in [prior work][prior work], where the null was reported only after correction for landing-spot quality.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the cut-versus-drive portability effect holds in the stated 2022-23 to 2025-26 NBA data. No record uses this data version, and the retrieved records do not state the same source or unit definitions.
Whether a 24-unit design has adequate power. None of [prior work] covers n=24, and the closest sample (n=92) is about four times larger.
The replication status of [prior work][prior work]. Its leave-one-out and permutation results are recorded, but no independent replication is recorded and its outcome is a derived delta.

Whether the portability outcome in SF-[prior work] can be reconstructed from the current per-game files. Data-catalog fields for mover identity, pre-move and post-move context, and destination quality were not checked.
The stability of the Spearman p=0 result in [prior work][prior work], which is recorded but not explained.
own_inferences: If the 24 units are team-seasons or single moves, the sample is too small to detect an effect of the size that the closest prior study reported (AUC about 0.65), let alone a smaller one.

Pooling to player-level mover-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26 would be needed to approach the 92-mover scale of [prior work][prior work], and the pooled design must address the same destination-quality confound recorded in [prior work][prior work].

Defining cut versus drive shares from the same play-by-play used to derive portability, or using post-move outcomes to choose the classification threshold, would create a circular label and inflate the apparent effect.
A cut-versus-drive classification rule must be fixed before outcomes are examined. Otherwise the tercile split in SF-[prior work] is a researcher degree of freedom.
uncertainties: The definition of the 24 units is not stated (player, team, move, or season-level), so the effective sample size is unknown.

Whether the NBA 2025-26 regular-season and playoff data used here is complete for the intended test. Per the stated availability, regular-season data is complete from 2026-04-13 and playoff data from 2026-06-21; earlier pulls would be partial.

The portability construct used in SF-[prior work] (an organizational function reproducing after a move) is not defined in the retrieved records, so it may not map onto the per-game variables available here.
Measurement reliability of the cut-share and drive-share classification from play-by-play action types and sub-types is not reported in any retrieved record.
No validation or replication status is recorded for SF-[prior work] beyond the auto-generated 'supported' label.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence showed that the closest prior study (SF-[prior work]) had a supported positive result, but at n=92, and that three related attempts were untestable because of power or sample problems. Together with the stated n=24, this moved the decision from a possible test of the question as posed to a do-not-proceed recommendation for the question as posed. The minimum viable test below is the only version that could be considered.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 units is far below the 92-mover sample of the closest prior study, and the related records were recorded as underpowered (MDE of 0.18 PPP at n=44). A test at n=24 cannot reliably detect an effect of the size previously reported.

Destination structural quality is recorded as a confounder ([prior work][prior work] null only after correction for landing-spot quality). Without a measure of destination quality the cut-versus-drive contrast is confounded with where players land.

Portability is a post-move delta. If the cut/drive classification or the portable/not-portable label is derived from the same outcome, the test is circular, as the tercile analysis in SF-[prior work] would be vulnerable to this.
The cut and drive shares depend on play-by-play action and sub-type coding. Their stability across seasons and across the playoff/regular-season split is not recorded in any retrieved record.

prior_work.summary: [prior work][prior work] reports a supported positive cut-share association with post-move portability in a 92-mover sample, which partly answers the question for a different sample and possibly a different outcome definition. The other three records are untestable for sample or power reasons and do not answer the question. Nothing retrieved tests the question with n=24 units or with the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data described here.

risks.text: n=24 units gives very low power. The closest prior study needed 92 movers, and related attempts with n=19 to 44 were recorded as underpowered.
Landing-spot quality and team context are recorded confounders. Without adjustment the cut-versus-drive effect may reflect where players moved rather than their role.
If the role classification or the portable label uses post-move outcomes, the association is partly built in.
Shares of cut and drive possessions from play-by-play coding may be unstable across seasons, and the playoff sample is smaller than the regular season.

The question is one of several role-type comparisons in this area, and the SF-[prior work] result depends on a choice of cut-minus-drive, tercile, and position splits. Without pre-specification the reported p-values are inflated.
The permutation test in SF-[prior work] used label shuffles. Its validity depends on whether shuffles preserve the dependence between roles, team and destination, so the placebo may be too weak.
Across 2022-23 to 2025-26, team-building, rule and pace changes may shift what cut and drive play types mean, so a pooled portability estimate could mix regimes.
The portable/not-portable label depends on how post-move function is defined; mislabeling of movers or misidentified role transitions would bias the contrast.

design.estimand: Difference in post-move portability (change in organizational function, Delta) between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, adjusted for pre-move role share and destination structural quality. This is a comparison of conditional associations, not a causal effect of role type.
design.unit: Player-move (mover-season). Only the player-level unit is considered here; team-season or single-game units would not reproduce the SF-[prior work] design.
design.sample: Not feasible with n=24. The minimum viable test requires pooling mover-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs to approach the scale of the closest prior study (n about 90 movers). If the pool falls well short, stop and report the question as untestable.
design.power: Pre-specify the MDE at 80% power before any outcome is examined, using the SD from the pooled sample. Based on SF-[prior work] (SD about 0.34), a 24-unit design has MDE well above any plausible effect. Proceed only if the pooled MDE is below the effect size reported in SF-[prior work] (AUC about 0.65, about one-third of a tercile difference).
design.controls: Destination structural quality (landing-spot net rating or structural-gap index measured before the move, not after); pre-move minutes and usage; team pace; position; season; and playoff versus regular-season indicator. Role classification thresholds fixed from pre-move data only, not from outcomes. Measurement reliability of cut and drive shares reported across seasons.
design.falsification: Placebo outcome: pre-move function delta (change in function before the move, when no move occurs). Permutation of portability labels preserving team and destination structure. Pre-specified negative control: the same cut-versus-drive contrast on non-movers should show no association.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (cut-minus-drive share vs portability). Tercile, position, and drop-one-player checks are secondary and are reported with Holm correction across the secondary set.
design.decision_rule: Support only if the pre-specified primary contrast is significant after Holm correction across the pre-registered secondary checks, the effect survives destination-quality adjustment, and the placebo and non-mover controls show no association. Reject if the pooled MDE is below the plausible effect and the observed effect is null. Report untestable if the pooled sample is below the MDE threshold.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Any pull before those completion dates is partial and must not be used. Derived play-type possession records must be rebuilt from play-by-play with a fixed coding version.
